diagnostic_evidence.quote: We insist on the fact that in the rows marked as `Hyperbolic' we used $\tau_{TTP'}^\theta$.
Comparison in terms of Time-to-Progression (TTP) between `On-Off'~AT and `Off-On'~AT.
The outcomes of `Off-On'~AT seem promising, as it shows an improvement in almost every performance indicator compared to `Off-On'~AT.

issues.failure_explanation: Progression is defined in eq:def_TTP as the first time n reaches 1.2 n_0, and MTD and `On-Off' AT are scored with that quantity; but the hyperbolic-cost schedule is scored with τ_TTP′ (disclosed only in the caption of table:Sum_Hyp) and `Off-On' AT is scored the same way without disclosure. The `Off-On' rule turns the drug on exactly when n ≥ 1.2 n_0, so its τ_TTP is the first trigger: with d_T̂ = 0 and u = 0 one has ṅ = (1−n)(s+r_R̂ r) ≥ 0.5 n(1−n), so the first trigger occurs within 18.6, 30 and 81 days for n_0 = 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, whereas table:Off-On reports minima of 107, 167 and 400 days. The tabulated quantity is therefore τ_TTP′, not the TTP of eq:def_TTP. By rmk:TTPvsTTP′, τ_TTP′ ≥ τ_TTP always, with strict inequality exactly when the trajectory returns below the threshold after reaching it — i.e. exactly for the two proposed schedules — so the substitution is systematically favourable to them and the claimed TTP gains are not like-for-like.

failure_location.quote: and on average it outperforms MTD and AT in terms of `time to progression' (see \cref{table:MTD_AT1,table:Sum_Hyp})

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Report τ_TTP and τ_TTP′ for every strategy and compare like with like (for MTD and `On-Off' AT the two coincide), label the substituted quantity as TTP′, and restate the conclusions as gains in time to irreversible progression, explicitly noting that the proposed schedules reach the progression threshold early and that the hyperbolic schedule underperforms for n_0 = 0.25.
issues.overall_effect: The headline claims that the hyperbolic-cost schedule and `Off-On' AT improve 'time to progression' over MTD and `On-Off' AT are unsupported: under eq:def_TTP both proposed policies progress at their first trigger/crossing, well before the benchmarks, and they keep the population at or above the progression threshold for extended periods. The introduction claim, the reading of the hyperbolic rows of table:Sum_Hyp, all of table:Off-On and the concluding claim of subsec:Off-On become unreliable; for n_0 = 0.25 the hyperbolic schedule is worse than the benchmarks even under τ_TTP′.
issues.title: Time-to-progression figures are TTP′ values reported and compared as TTP
issues.why_classification: A consistent use of TTP′ leaves all tables and comparisons essentially intact (benchmarks have τ_TTP = τ_TTP′), so no new computation or argument is needed; but the advertised 'time to progression' superiority must be withdrawn and replaced by a weaker claim about a non-clinical surrogate, a limited weakening that still leaves a recognizably comparable result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \dot r_u^\theta(\tau) = \hat r_R \big( 1 - s_u^\theta(\tau) - r_u^\theta(\tau) \big) r_u^\theta(\tau) - \hat d_T r_u^\theta(\tau),
and we can deduce that the set $\Delta_1$ is invariant.

issues.failure_explanation: On Δ_1 (where s = 0) the model gives ṙ = r( r_R̂(1−r) − d_T̂ ), which changes sign at r* = (r_R̂−d_T̂)/r_R̂ when d_T̂ < r_R̂ and is negative for every r > 0 when d_T̂ ≥ r_R̂; it never changes sign at r_R̂/(r_R̂+d_T̂). E.g. for r_R̂ = 1, d_T̂ = 1 one gets ṙ = −r² < 0 on all of (0,1/2], contradicting the asserted ṙ ≥ 0 there, and the degenerate case d_T̂ ≥ r_R̂ is not covered at all. The case split that is claimed to yield invariance of Δ_1 is therefore false as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the threshold by the correct root r* = (r_R̂−d_T̂)/r_R̂ and treat d_T̂ ≥ r_R̂ separately, or delete the split and invoke only the boundary signs, which already prove invariance of Δ_1.
issues.overall_effect: Only the intermediate sign split on the face s = 0 is wrong; invariance of Δ (and hence the truncation construction and lem:extension, which are used downstream) still follows from the boundary signs ṙ = 0 at r = 0 and ṙ = −d_T̂ ≤ 0 at r = 1, so no downstream result is lost.
issues.title: False monotonicity threshold in the invariance proof on the face s = 0
issues.why_classification: A one-line local correction of a single proof step restores the argument; the lemma statement, its conclusion and every dependent result keep their full strength, with no new lemma or construction needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we discretized the interval $[0.5,1]$ where $\hat r_R$ varies into $25$ equi\-spaced nodes with distance $0.02$
into $49$ nodes with a constant step equal to $0.002$
which has a support consisting of $N=1225$ points

issues.failure_explanation: The listed grid {0.5, 0.52, …, 1} contains 26 nodes (step 0.02 over an interval of length 0.5) and {0.002, 0.004, …, 0.1} contains 50 nodes (step 0.002 up to 0.1), while the weights are 1/25 and 1/49, the indices run over j = 1..25 and k = 1..49, and N = 25·49 = 1225 is asserted. The node sets, the node counts and the weights are mutually incompatible, so μ_N (and Θ_N) is not well defined; the second grid is moreover said to subdivide the interval [0.002,1] although the target law is U(0.002,0.1). Different repairs give genuinely different ensembles.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Fix one consistent grid (e.g. the 25 nodes 0.5,…,0.98 and the 49 nodes 0.002,…,0.098, or the 26- and 50-node grids including the right endpoints) and state the nodes, the weights and N accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The ensemble over which every running cost is averaged and over which all max/min/mean TTP statistics of tables table:MTD_AT1, table:Sum_Hyp and table:Off-On are computed is ambiguous; the computed schedules and all reported statistics cannot be reproduced until the grid is fixed.
issues.title: The discrete ensemble measure μ_N is defined with incompatible node sets, counts and weights
issues.why_classification: Selecting a consistent grid is a short local edit with a choice between equivalent repairs; the optimization method, the metrics and the qualitative conclusions are preserved unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: This phenomenon is since, throughout the iterations of the gradient descent $k=0,\ldots,500$, $\nabla_{u_k^1} \J^1(\tau)$ and $\nabla_{u_k^2} \J^2(\tau)$ are small when $\tau$ is close to $T$.
the resolution of an ensemble optimal control problem tends automatically to find the interval where the decision-making on the therapy schedule has the most significant effect

issues.failure_explanation: What the remark claims is that the flat tail of the computed controls certifies that T has been chosen large enough, and that the minimization thereby 'automatically finds' the decision-relevant interval. What the paper establishes is only that ∇_uJ(τ) is small for τ close to T, and this is forced for every control, every cost, every ensemble and every horizon by the terminal condition g_u^θ(T) = (0,0) of eq:grad_back_ode: eq:grad_rep gives ∇_uJ(τ) = O(T−τ). A short remaining integration interval makes late decisions irrelevant for any integral cost, so the observed flatness occurs verbatim even when T is far too short and carries no information about whether the tumors have saturated or whether the horizon is adequate.

failure_location.quote: We can use this phenomenon as an empirical test for deciding whether the time horizon $T$ has been appropriately set large (see \cref{rmk:choice_T}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the gradient-tail test and weaken rmk:choice_T to declare T_hor a modelling choice, or replace the test with a genuine verification (e.g. insensitivity of the optimal value to T, or a proof that the ensemble has reached its equilibrium on the tail).
issues.overall_effect: The stated validation of the horizons of table:Time_horizon and the claim of rmk:choice_T that their arbitrariness is benign rest on a test with no discriminating power; the optimization scheme, the computed schedules and the strategy comparisons themselves are unaffected.
issues.title: The proposed test that the horizon T is large enough is vacuous
issues.why_classification: Only an auxiliary justification is withdrawn, by a short local edit; the method, the computed schedules, the metrics and every reported comparison survive unchanged, so no new argument or recomputation is required.
